ἐναλλ-άσσω , Att.
ἐνάλλ-ττω , pf.
A. “ἐνήλλαχα”
Plb. 6.43.2
, Phld. Mus. p.73K. :—exchange, φόνον θανάτῳ ἐ., i.e. pay for murder by death,
E. Andr. 1028 (lyr.); μεταβολὰς ἐ. undergo changes, Plb. l.c.; παντοίας μορφὰς ἐ. to assume . ., Apollod. 2.5.11 : c. inf., ἐνήλλαξεν θεὸς τὴν τοῦδ᾽ ὕβριν πρὸς μῆλα . . πεσεῖν turned aside, diverted his fury so as to fall upon the sheep, S. Aj. 1060 .
2. cross, “τὼ πόδε”
Philostr. Im. 2.7
; also intr., cross one another, of veins and arteries, Arist. PA 668b21 .
3. Astrol., exchange domicile, of planets, Vett.Val. 73.15 .
4. ἐχρῆν ἐνηλλαχέναι one should have reversed the statement, Phld. l.c.
II. give in exchange, “τιἀντί τινος”
App. BC 3.27
, 5.12 :— Med. , receive in exchange, τί δ᾽ ἐνήλλακται τῆς ἡμερίας νὺξ ἥδε βάρος; what heavy change from the day hath this night received? S. Aj. 208 , cf. Ph. 2.638 .
III.
Pass. , to be interarticulated, “ἄρθρα ἐνηλλαγμένα”
Hp. Art. 46
; also τὸ μέτρον τοῖς δισυλλάβοις ἐναλλάσσεται the metre employs the various disyllabic feet interchangeably, Anon.Metr. Oxy. 220 iii 13 .
2. have commercial relations with, “ὅσοι Ἀθηναίοις ἤδη ἐνηλλάγησαν”
Th. 1.120
.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
